classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate and factor to locate turning points, then select the outer monotonic branches matching the prescribed interval forms.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $f$ is restricted to $(-\infty,A]$, find the largest possible $A$ so that the inverse function $f^{-1}$ exists.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2-6x-9\\f'(x)&=3(x+1)(x-3)\end{align*}$$
The stationary points occur at $x=-1$ and $x=3$. The graph increases up to $x=-1$, then decreases. The largest one-to-one interval of the required form is $(-\infty,-1]$, so $A=-1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $f$ is restricted to $[B,\infty)$, find the smallest possible $B$ so that the inverse function $f^{-1}$ exists.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2-6x-9\\f'(x)&=3(x+1)(x-3)\end{align*}$$
The stationary points occur at $x=-1$ and $x=3$. The graph decreases on $[-1,3]$ and increases on $[3,\infty)$. The largest one-to-one interval of the required form is $[3,\infty)$, so $B=3$.
